Plan power and sample size for a Pearson HWE test

Source: R/hwe_diagnostic.R
hwe_power.Rd

Compute prospective power or the minimum whole-number sample size for the ordinary, uncorrected Pearson Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE) test. This is a noncentral chi-square planning approximation for independently sampled diploid individuals at one biallelic autosomal locus.

Usage

hwe_power(
  N,
  alpha = 0.05,
  genotype_probs = NULL,
  allele_frequency = NULL,
  misclassification_matrix = NULL
)

hwe_mssn(
  target_power = 0.8,
  alpha = 0.05,
  genotype_probs = NULL,
  allele_frequency = NULL,
  misclassification_matrix = NULL
)

Arguments

N

Number of analyzable individuals, a positive whole number at most 2^52.

alpha

Nominal significance level, strictly between 0 and 1.

genotype_probs

Assumed observed probabilities for genotypes with 0, 1, and 2 copies of the same allele. Supply a finite, nonnegative vector summing to 1, or instead supply both allele_frequency and misclassification_matrix. Names, if given, must be "0", "1", and "2" in that order.

allele_frequency

Frequency of the counted allele before error, in [0, 1]. It defines the true HWE probabilities.

misclassification_matrix

Numeric 3 by 3 matrix with rows for true genotype and columns for observed genotype, both in 0, 1, 2 allele-copy order. Any row or column names must be "0", "1", "2" in that order. Entry [i + 1, j + 1] is the probability of calling j copies when there are truly i copies. Each row sums to 1. Multiplying the true probability row vector by this matrix gives the observed probabilities.

target_power

Desired rejection probability, strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

A list with the sample size N, achieved power, alpha, df, critical_value, lambda (the noncentrality parameter), lambda_per_person, expected_counts, sparse_expected, true_genotype_probs (matrix scenario only), observed_probs, fitted allele_frequency, expected_probs, and F. hwe_mssn() also returns target_power and previous_power at the immediately smaller positive size when available. An equilibrium alternative has power alpha at every size in this approximation. For such an alternative and target above alpha, N is Inf and achieved power and size-dependent diagnostics are NA.

Details

The fitted null uses the counted-allele frequency from the assumed observed probabilities g. Write h for the HWE probabilities at that frequency. The noncentrality parameter is lambda = N * sum((g - h)^2 / h) = N * F^2, where F = 1 - g[2] / h[2] uses the heterozygote probabilities. Power is the upper-tail probability under this one-degree-of-freedom noncentral chi-square at the central chi-square cutoff. No exact-test power or goodness of fit to a fixed external frequency is calculated. The fitted distribution must contain both alleles. Expected counts below five trigger a warning for finite designs. They are a diagnostic for the approximation, rather than a constraint in the sample-size search. Sample sizes above 2^52 are outside the supported whole-number range.

References

Rohlfs RV, Weir BS (2008). Distributions of Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium test statistics. Genetics 180(3), 1609-1616. doi:10.1534/genetics.108.088005 .

See also

hwe_test()

Examples

g <- c(0.35588, 0.48424, 0.15988)
hwe_power(1000, genotype_probs = g)$power
#> [1] 0.05591224
hwe_mssn(genotype_probs = g)$N
#> [1] 152612
